A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same EIFBENCH and SegPO study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison, including identification of material removed from v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, SegPO-versus-GRPO experiments, human agreement measurements, sensitivity analyses, and an alternative-judge evaluation.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark, training, and validation results and adds evaluations of Gemini-2.0-Flash and DeepSeek-V3.

M1.justification: The corrected ILA definition removes inverse constraint-count weighting. Because ILA enters SegPO's global reward in Equation (10), this changes the reward as formally specified. The global/segment advantage procedure and training template remain unchanged; implementation changes or retraining are not established.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,000-instance, predominantly Chinese benchmark: 450 plain-text, 450 dyadic-dialogue, and 100 multi-party-dialogue instances, covering the same eight task categories. Added models and the removed alternative judge do not change dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 4 adds Gemini-2.0-Flash and DeepSeek-V3, expanding from 18 to 20 model configurations. Gemini-2.0-Flash previously appeared as an evaluator, not an evaluated model. Table 5 retains the same base-model and GRPO comparators for SegPO.

E3.justification: Equation (1) changes a central evaluation metric: v1 weights each fully satisfied instruction by 1/c_i,j, whereas v2 averages unweighted instruction-success indicators. v2 also removes the Gemini-2.0-Flash judging protocol from Appendix C.2. These substantially change the documented scoring and evaluation design, although retained scores are unchanged and reruns are not established.

E4.justification: v2 removes Appendix C.2 and Table 9, eliminating the complete alternative-judge analysis of whether benchmark findings persist under Gemini-2.0-Flash. This removes a distinct robustness check. The instruction/constraint sensitivity plots, full-constraint satisfaction analysis, and human validation remain.

E5.justification: The PCC and kappa estimation procedures and reporting in Tables 6–7 are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for model performance.

E6.justification: v2 removes all 108 alternative-judge scores in Table 9 and adds 12 scores in Table 4. The new plain-text ILA/CLA results are 0.2291/0.7028 for Gemini-2.0-Flash and 0.1955/0.6836 for DeepSeek-V3. All retained Table 4 scores and the SegPO comparison in Table 5 are unchanged; the removed scores used a different judge.

T1.justification: Equation (1) removes the extra 1/c_i,j factor, making ILA mathematically consistent with the stated fraction of instructions satisfying every constraint. This is a substantive but localized definition correction. The remaining GRPO/SegPO mathematics and Appendix B are unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction expands the claimed empirical contribution from analyzing 18 LLMs to 20. The central EIFBENCH and SegPO contributions, abstract, conclusion, and claimed 14.85% and 3.40% improvements remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.3.1 replaces general observations about competitive reasoning models with claims of substantially superior ILA and deeper understanding enabled by specialized architecture. v2 also removes the assertion that alternative-judge evaluations generally agree with GPT-4o. The stated language-coverage and task-dependency limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 5.2 adds Tongyi-CCAI/Complex-IF as a second code/data access location while retaining Hope-Rita/EIFBench. Hardware, inference framework, timing information, and Appendix E prompts are unchanged. The PDFs document an additional access route, not verified changes in resource availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations concerning conversation analysis, DEMO dialogue processing, evaluator fairness and instruction-following assessment, adaptive thinking, and DeepSeek-V3. These provide localized contextual support; Section 6 and the central positioning against earlier instruction-following benchmarks remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized edits to data-collection and evaluation prose, rewrites the open-model interpretation in Section 5.3.1, adds acknowledgments, and removes Appendix C.2. The overall narrative structure and extensive prompt appendix remain stable.

P2.justification: Table 4 gains two rows, Table 9 is removed, and Table 5 moves from page 7 to page 8 with accompanying text reflow. The figures and remaining table structures are retained, without a substantial visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 fixes an important inconsistency in the ILA definition and adds useful model comparisons and access information. However, it removes the alternative-judge evidence and strengthens reasoning-model interpretations beyond consistently supported findings: Table 4 gives Qwen3-32B plain-text ILA of 0.2050 versus 0.2073 without thinking. These gains in correctness and coverage coexist with reduced validation and less cautious interpretation, leaving the net quality direction uncertain.
